## Games

### Niners Chemnitz secure second season win against MHP RIESEN Ludwigsburg

*Played Saturday, 31 October 2026* *(updated with new sources)*

Niners Chemnitz secured their second season win in the BBL with a 94:78 victory over MHP RIESEN Ludwigsburg on October 31. The home team, who had just 72 hours earlier defeated EuroCup titleholders Bourg-en-Bresse 96:77, dominated the game after a slow start. Nighael Ceaser led the Niners with 19 points and 6 rebounds, while Thomas Rutherford scored 19 points and grabbed 15 rebounds for Ludwigsburg. The Niners' second win of the season comes after a string of five losses in the BBL, but they have been more successful in the EuroCup and Netto BBL Cup, where they have won six of seven games. The team's coach, Rodrigo Pastore, was able to distribute playing time evenly among his players, with seven of them scoring between 8 and 11 points in the game against Bourg-en-Bresse.

## Around the League

### Rasta Vechta's Unsung Heroes: Team Manager and Physiotherapist

Rasta Vechta's professional basketball team relies not only on its players, but also on its dedicated support staff. Team Manager Max Plate, 20, is the team's jack-of-all-trades, responsible for tasks such as preparing the locker room, receiving opponents, and even printing warm-up shirts. Plate has developed a pre-game ritual of hanging the players' jerseys on wooden hangers, a superstition he believes brings him good luck. Meanwhile, Physiotherapist Beatriz Santos, 28, is responsible for taping the players' ankles to prevent injuries. With a high level of precision, she bandages each player every five minutes, a task she has mastered over her three years with the team. Santos notes that working with professional athletes is particularly challenging due to their high expectations and need to perform at their best without injury.

Sources:

### Ratiopharm Ulm defeat Baskets Oldenburg 81-65 in heated BBL game

Ratiopharm Ulm secured a convincing 81-65 win over Baskets Oldenburg in their latest BBL encounter. The game was marked by a series of intense moments, including a 6-0 Ulm blitz in the third quarter that forced Oldenburg to take a timeout. Despite a strong start from Oldenburg, Ulm's defense improved significantly in the second quarter, leading to a 44-32 halftime lead. Oldenburg struggled to get close to the basket, and Ulm's offense found its rhythm, with Devin Schmidt's three-pointer bringing life back to the game. In the final quarter, Oldenburg's team was plagued by fouls, with four players committing five fouls, including a disqualifying foul by Pope. The win sees Ulm move on to their next match, an away game against Rostock on Saturday, while Oldenburg will play their next game.

### BonnRhöndorf win inaugural JBBL-Ligapokal title

The BonnRhöndorf team, a cooperation between Telekom Baskets Bonn and Dragons Rhöndorf, won the inaugural JBBL-Ligapokal title with a 99-78 victory over ALBA Berlin in the final. The game was played in front of around 200 spectators at the Baskets Ausbildungszentrum. BonnRhöndorf dominated the game from the start, leading 25-13 after the first quarter and 57-34 at halftime. They continued to build on their lead throughout the game, eventually winning the title with a 20-point margin. This is the second national title won by the BonnRhöndorf team this year, following their win in the German U16 championship in May. The JBBL-Ligapokal is a new competition, making BonnRhöndorf's win a historic first title in the Jugend Basketball Bundesliga.
